body: ## Columns
`request_id`, `timestamp` (UTC), `model`, `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `billed_tokens`, `project`.
## Common reasons a customer's own total differs from the export
- A project filter left on.
- A local timezone used to cut the month.
- Counting `prompt_tokens` only.

- customers see a successful HTTP status but the stream ends without an explicit termination signal and without consistent client-visible error handling, or
- the customer provides multiple request IDs showing premature termination correlated with new overload reasons.
---
## What Support should ask for (intake checklist)
Request the following in the initial reply to reduce ping-pong:
1) Affected route(s): e.g., `/v1/chat/completions`
2) Region/endpoint base URL (if multi-region)
3) Time window (with timezone) and approximate request rate
4) Sample `x-redwood-request-id` values (3–10 IDs)
5) Full 429 response headers + body (raw)
6) Whether they are using streaming
7) Their current retry policy (backoff, max attempts, concurrency)
8) Whether it’s isolated to a single API key or all keys in the account
Internal-only (if available to TAM/CS): contract tier (Hosted API vs Dedicated), priority class, and any approved exceptions.

{"name": "team-handoff", "steps": "1. Decide whether a case is needed at all. search_knowledge for the routing policy covering this request (e.g. "billing case routing <topic>", "who approves <request>"). If a current page says Support answers this without a case (an explanation, a general rule, "your account team confirms your terms"), answer and stop.
2. Pick the owning team from the current routing/approval documents, not from old drafts or threads. Use the console account (plan, channel, contracts) to choose between rows, e.g. self-serve vs signed contract, direct vs marketplace/reseller. If the developer claims something the console doesn't show (a contract, a plan), route per the policy for that situation.
3. Collect the intake the receiving team needs (the routing page lists it per row) with one ask_developer call: e.g. invoice_id, line_items, amounts, request_ids, time_of_issue together with timezone, error_code, checks_done, contract. If they don't have something, hand off anyway and record it as "not provided" (not as a negative answer).
4. Do any permitted write first (credit note or dispute), because escalation closes the console.
5. confirm_with_developer: "Hand this to <team> with <one-line summary>." If no, don't escalate; tell them what they can do instead.
6. escalate_case with: team; summary (what they asked, what the console shows, what the team must decide/do); details with every fact given (ids, amounts as the console shows them, UTC window, request ids, the amount requested if any, what's missing); dispute_id if any. Never include card numbers.
7. Tell the developer: anything the policy row says to tell the customer (e.g. a rule that applies to their plan or channel), which team has it, the case id, and what that team will do next. No promised outcome, amount or date; no internal credit tables or ranges."}
